newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine government appeals telephone ruling.
newsitem.headline: Argentine government appeals telephone ruling.

text.p: The Argentine government Wednesday appealed a judge's ruling that suspended rate hikes on local telephone calls, the state news agency Telam reported.
A federal judge last week suspended a decree on the new rate structure pending the outcome of a suit brought by the nation's Ombudsman to have the changes reversed.
The government late in January authorized the changes, which increased the cost of local calls and telephone rentals, but slashed the rates for national and international long- distance calls.
Telefonica de Argentina and Telecom Argentina had waged a long hard lobbying campaign for the rate changes, which they said would make charges fairer for provincial businesses.
They also hoped it would prepare them for the opening of the Argentine phone market to competition, probably in the year 2000.

But consumer groups and opposition parties fought hard against the charges and argued in public hearings ending in December 1996 that private users' telephone bills would rise and the phone companies pocket the difference.
The companies argued the new charges would not increase their profits. Telefonica is controlled by Telefonica de Espana, and Telecom by France Telecom.
